quote: I have suffered, like other writers, from indolence, irresolution, distaste to my work, absence of “inspiration,” and all that: but I have also found that sitting down, however reluctantly, with the pen in my hand, I have never worked for one quarter of an hour without finding myself in full train.
source: Harriet Martineau, Autobiography, vol. 1, Fourth Period, section I, p. 144 (ed. Maria Weston Chapman, 1877)

evidence.where: archive.org full text (djvu OCR) of the Cornell copy, volume one, fourth edition; the passage read in place with the running head “144 AUTOBIOGRAPHY. [1832.” above it and “Aged 30.] TIMES OF WORKING. 145” after it
evidence.edition: Harriet Martineau’s Autobiography, ed. Maria Weston Chapman, vol. 1 (Boston: James R. Osgood, 1877; read in the fourth edition, Houghton, Osgood and Company, 1879)
evidence.locator: Vol. 1, Fourth Period (To the Age of Thirty-Seven), section I, p. 144, in the paragraph beginning “One deep and steady conviction”

reason: The words are Martineau’s exactly, on p. 144 as proposed. Her sentence runs on after a second colon (“so that all the quarter hours, arguings, doubtings and hesitation … I now regard as so much waste”); the card stops at that colon with a full stop and alters no word, the same clause-boundary cut February accepted. Fame rests on reference use (the line is a staple of writers’ routine anthologies), which is the editor’s call. Not shipped, unused, not banned.
